content:
BERT and GPT are both Transformer-based language models, but they are designed for different purposes and trained differently.

| Feature | BERT | GPT |
|---|---|---|
| Full name | Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers | Generative Pre-trained Transformer |
| Transformer type | Encoder-only | Decoder-only |
| Training style | Predicts masked words in a sentence | Predicts the next word/token |
| Direction | Bidirectional: looks at both left and right context | Unidirectional/autoregressive: looks at previous tokens only |
| Main strength | Understanding text | Generating text |
| Common tasks | Classification, sentiment analysis, question answering, named entity recognition | Chatbots, writing, summarization, code generation, creative text |
| Example use | “Is this review positive or negative?” | “Write an email about this topic.” |

### Simple explanation

**BERT** is better at understanding existing text.  
For example, if given:

> “The bank was closed because it was a holiday.”

BERT uses words before and after “bank” to understand that it probably means a financial institution.

**GPT** is better at producing new text.  
For example, if given:

> “Once upon a time…”

GPT predicts what should come next and continues the story.

### Training difference

BERT is trained with **masked language modeling**:

> “The cat sat on the [MASK].”

It learns to predict:

> “mat”

GPT is trained with **next-token prediction**:

> “The cat sat on the”

It predicts the next likely word:

> “mat”

### In short

**BERT = text understanding**  
**GPT = text generation**
